chains.title: GATA3 binds the ref GATA motif and activates LMO1

links.claim: GATA3 binds the ref C allele more strongly than alt A. On the LMO1 minus strand, ref C corresponds to G and alt A to T; the ref allele preserves a GATA motif, while the protective alt allele creates a TATA-like sequence. GATA3 is chosen because it is occupied at the variant in SK-N-SH and the literature directly reports that the protective TATA allele ablates GATA3 binding. No QBiC-SELEX model/data for GATA3 is supplied in this evidence set.
rs2168101 lies in EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, consistent with an active regulatory element.

The variant is in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from the TSS; credible-set L2G maps the association best to LMO1, the GTEx eQTL reports lower LMO1 expression for alt A relative to ref C, and the protective TATA allele is associated with decreased total LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma primary tumours.

GATA3 is occupied at this element in SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells and is expressed there; GATA3 is also linked to neuroblastoma super-enhancer and adrenergic-lineage biology, supporting a cell-type-compatible route.

The ref GATA allele is associated with higher LMO1 and increased adrenergic neuroblastoma risk, whereas the protective alt TATA allele ablates GATA3 binding, lowers LMO1 expression, and reduces MYCN-driven tumor penetrance in the zebrafish knock-in model.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP-qPCR shows preferential GATA3 occupancy on ref C over alt A in SK-N-SH.

chains.title: GATA2 binds the ref GATA motif as an alternative related factor and activates LMO1

links.claim: GATA2 is an alternative GATA-family factor at this motif: it is occupied at the variant in SK-N-SH and the ref C allele preserves the GATA motif, so GATA2 is predicted to bind ref C more strongly than alt A. However, there is no QBiC-SELEX model/data for GATA2 in this evidence set, and no allele-specific GATA2 binding is shown; direct literature instead reports GATA3 binding ablation for the protective allele, making GATA2 the weaker competing factor.
rs2168101 lies in EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, consistent with an active regulatory element.

The variant is in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from the TSS; credible-set L2G maps the association best to LMO1, and the GTEx eQTL reports lower LMO1 expression for alt A relative to ref C, supporting allele-dependent LMO1 regulation.

GATA2 is occupied at this element in SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells and is highly expressed there; GATA2 is also reported in neuroblastoma differentiation TF waves, making this cell type plausible for a GATA2-mediated effect.

If GATA2 were the functional factor, the ref GATA allele would be associated with higher LMO1 and increased adrenergic neuroblastoma risk, while the alt TATA allele would lower LMO1 and be protective. The GATA-family and locus-level literature supports this direction, but the evidence is not GATA2-specific.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP-qPCR shows preferential GATA2 occupancy on ref C over alt A in SK-N-SH.
GATA2 knockdown or CRISPRi reduces ref-allele enhancer activity and LMO1 expression more than alt-allele activity.
GATA2 occupancy at this element is stronger in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells than in non-neural cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 occupancy at rs2168101 is absent or opposite in SK-N-SH cells.
GATA2 knockdown does not affect ref-vs-alt enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
GATA3, not GATA2, accounts for all allele-specific GATA-family occupancy and activity at this site.

grades_v0.reason: GATA2 occupancy in SK-N-SH is shown by ChIP peaks, but no allele-specific GATA2 binding or QBiC-SELEX change is supplied.
